title: The Fifth Floor
genre: light mystery with humor, everyday Baku life, a media-company workplace
premise: Sevda, 28, works at a small media company in Baku. After she locks herself out one night, a quiet neighbor from the fifth floor, Murad, helps her with a ladder. Small strange things start to happen in the building, and every episode ends with a question the learner answers. Warm, funny, a little mysterious. No violence, politics, religion or brands.

characters.name: Sevda
characters.role: main character, 28, works at a media company, a bit clumsy, curious, kind. She is also the coach who reacts to the learner's answers on the page.

characters.name: Murad
characters.role: neighbor on the fifth floor, quiet, keeps a ladder in the basement, knows everyone in the building

characters.name: Aunt Zarifa
characters.role: elderly neighbor on the first floor, knows every rumor, loves tea

characters.name: Kamran
characters.role: Sevda's colleague at the media company, jokes a lot

characters.name: Locksmith
characters.role: the night locksmith Sevda called in episode 1; may return

characters.name: Leyla
characters.role: Sevda's editor at the media company, strict but fair, loves a good headline

rules: One episode per day. The episode is the lesson's story in content/<DATE>.json and must still follow routine/daily-content.md (all new words appear, glossary complete).
Start each episode with a one-sentence reminder of what happened before, woven into the text.

End each episode with a cliffhanger and 2-3 choices (play/days/<DATE>.json). The next episode follows the choice the learner made (read from the artifact database). If no choice was made, pick the first one.
Use the learner's mission sentences from the previous day when natural (a character can say or think them), and give one short friendly feedback line on them in play/days/<DATE>.json 'feedback'.
Keep the overall mystery slow: one small clue per episode, resolve it after about 10-14 episodes, then start a new storyline with the same people.

episodes.title: Locked Out
episodes.summary: Sevda locks herself out at midnight, calls a locksmith, and is rescued by Murad from the fifth floor, who holds a ladder while she climbs to her balcony. She cancels the locksmith and now keeps a spare key at her mother's.
episodes.cliffhanger: The next morning Sevda finds a note under her door: 'You left something on the balcony.' But she is sure she left nothing there.

choices.text: Go up to the fifth floor and ask Murad about the note.
Ignore the note and hurry to work.

episodes.title: The Note
episodes.summary: Murad says the note is not in his handwriting and suggests someone from the building group chat, where Aunt Zarifa posts everything. At work, editor Leyla asks Sevda to write an article about building group chats. In the evening Sevda finds a small wooden box on her balcony with an old key labeled 'Basement, room 3'.
episodes.cliffhanger: Sevda has a mysterious key labeled 'Basement, room 3'. What should she do with it?

choices.text: Ask Aunt Zarifa. She knows every story in the building.
Post a photo of the box in the building's group chat.
Go down to the basement and try the key in room 3.

episodes.title: Aunt Zarifa's Tea
episodes.summary: Aunt Zarifa recognizes the key: it belonged to Mr. Bahram, a watchmaker and the former owner of Sevda's apartment, who loved secrets and riddles and moved away when he retired in 1998, promising to leave a hint for the next kind owner. Room 3 in the basement was his workshop and nobody has opened it for years; Sevda needs permission from the building manager, Mr. Tofig. Zarifa gives Sevda an unsigned envelope addressed only to her apartment number.
episodes.cliffhanger: An envelope with only Sevda's apartment number on it. What should she do?

choices.text: Open the envelope right now, in front of Aunt Zarifa.
Take it home and open it alone.
Go to Mr. Tofig first and ask for permission to open room 3.

episodes.title: The Clock That Never Moves
episodes.summary: Sevda opens the envelope at Aunt Zarifa's: a riddle signed 'B.' says 'Find the clock that never moves, and the door will open.' Zarifa compares it with the back of an old framed photo and is certain it is Mr. Bahram's handwriting, so he must still be alive. The envelope appeared in Zarifa's mailbox very early; Sevda remembers the lobby clock, stuck at a quarter past seven for years.
episodes.cliffhanger: The lobby clock has been stuck for years. What should Sevda do?

choices.text: Check the old clock in the lobby right away.
Ask Mr. Tofig for permission and open room 3 first.
Show the riddle to Murad. He knows everyone in the building.
